redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Light check surfaced a clearly authoritative and directly on-point source: the DPI Map country profile for Gambia (last updated 01/10/2024) explicitly records 'Regulation for digital ID: NO'. This is corroborated by the Gambia National Digital Identity Strategy document (UNECA-hosted; part of the 2023-2028 Digital ID Transformation Strategy) which lists 'strengthening legal and regulatory frameworks to support digital identity management' as a forward-looking action item rather than describing existing digital ID-specific regulation. Gambia's 2025 Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act is a general data protection law (not digital ID-specific) and does not change this assessment. The row was mislabelled as Unknown; recalculated to 1 (No) per the variable scale (0=Unknown; 1=No; 2=Yes).
revised_comments: No specific regulation or policy addresses digital identity in the Gambia beyond general identification legislation. The Gambia National Digital ID and Digital Transformation Strategy (2023-2028) identifies the strengthening of legal and regulatory frameworks for digital identity as a planned future action rather than an existing instrument. A general Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act was passed by the National Assembly in 2025 but this addresses data protection broadly and is not specific to digital identity.
